source.title: Domain-Independent Dominance of Adaptive Methods
source.authors: P. Savarese; David A. McAllester; Sudarshan Babu; M. Maire

record.tranche_reason: Reports optimizer comparisons on image and language tasks that refine V4: with extensive tuning, Adam and other adaptive methods can match or outperform SGD on several benchmarks; Adam performs better on word-level Penn Treebank in the reported comparison.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own benchmark results comparing optimizers and its CIFAR adaptability sweep. The synthetic convergence experiment concerns convergence to a stationary point, not the claim’s train/test generalization gap, so it is not included. Hyperparameter values from heatmaps are not transcribed as separate results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD. Its extensive learning-rate and epsilon searches test V4's qualification that broader tuning can remove or reverse an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: jointly tuning learning rate and adaptability lets Adam and AvaGrad outperform SGD on all four reported benchmarks, while AvaGrad makes that search more separable. Correct the record's word-level characterization to character-level Penn Treebank. The conclusion concerns selected methods, not every adaptive optimizer.
record.recipe_differences: The paper tests optimizer choices and hyperparameter tuning on benchmark tasks, rather than comparing train/test gaps under the original optimizer studies’ protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: The better optimizer and relative results vary by dataset, architecture, and learning-rate/adaptability settings. On image classification the optimal adaptability parameter is relatively large; on Penn Treebank it is small. The study states AvaGrad’s learning rate is less coupled to adaptability than Adam’s.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic example and convergence proofs concern reaching stationary points; hyperparameter separability concerns search cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Delayed adaptive updates can improve stationary-point convergence, and AvaGrad can reduce coupling between learning rate and epsilon.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 optimizer advantage is explicitly called inconclusive because adaptive methods were evaluated at more hyperparameter settings. CIFAR table entries report standard deviations over 3 runs; ImageNet and Penn Treebank table entries report no uncertainty. The study compares held-out metrics but does not report training error, so it cannot directly assess the train/test gap described in V4.
record.rows_left_out: The CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet 28-4 hyperparameter search is represented by aggregate textual findings only, not individual heatmap cells; the authors report 441 settings per adaptive method and identify optimal values and validation outcomes but do not give each cell numerically in the supplied text. The 3-layer LSTM with 300 hidden units is a validation hyperparameter sweep and is not extracted as a separate benchmark row.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
A width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate; using two widths for hyperparameter transfer does not test this.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

A controlled limited-tuning versus broader-tuning comparison with equal search budgets; equal or better training performance despite worse held-out performance; switching Adam to SGD; word-level language modelling. Decay schedules and weight-decay strengths are not broadly swept.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Controlled dropout comparisons; dropout is part of the language-model recipe, not an experimental contrast.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with measured generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States use adaptive-worse as the reference direction; a reversed state can support V4's explicit broader-tuning qualification. CIFAR results have standard deviations over three runs but no significance tests; ImageNet and Penn Treebank report no uncertainty. The paper does not measure training-versus-test gaps, but its held-out optimizer comparisons directly test V4. The explicitly omitted validation sweeps need no missing entries. The study's proposed optimizers remain relevant because their benchmark rows measure the same held-out optimizer comparison named by V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.

The study compares optimizers on specific benchmarks, but does not compare their training performance against test performance or report whether differences persist under broader tuning beyond its own hyperparameter searches.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the train/test gap.
